_about: Export presets for arsenal.media.export (promoted from the studio's production-pipeline export_presets.json, 2026-10-12). Numbers cite their source in 'why'. Loudness targets are applied by a measured two-pass loudnorm whose output is read back, never by a fixed gain. 'measured' rows are this machine's runs of tests/test_arsenal_media_export.py on a 10 s synthetic excerpt.

_sources.youtube_upload: https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/1722171 (H.264 High, 2 B-frames, CABAC, closed GOP of half the frame rate, 4:2:0, BT.709, AAC-LC or Opus 48 kHz, stereo 384 kbps, 2160p60 SDR 53-68 Mbps, moov atom at front)
_sources.youtube_loudness: YouTube turns down audio louder than about -14 LUFS and does not turn up quieter audio (no official Google page; see https://workflow.frame.io/guide/loudness-for-youtube and verify with Stats for nerds 'Volume / Normalized')
_sources.shorts: 1080x1920 9:16, up to 3 min since Oct 2024 (https://riverside.com/blog/how-long-can-youtube-shorts-be); A/B title/thumbnail tests do NOT run on Shorts (https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/16391400)
_sources.true_peak_margin: TP set to -1.5 dBTP (not -1.0): first test render measured -0.9 dBTP after AAC encode with a -1.0 target (test/shorts_test.mp4.json)

youtube_4k60.why: Final long-form upload. 2160p gets YouTube's VP9/AV1 ladder (widely reported, not an official Google statement), and the 4K master leaves room for 2x punch-ins from a 4K capture. CRF 16 x264 'slow' lands above Google's 53-68 Mbps table on busy League frames; the 9950X3D encodes it in software.

measured.excerpt: 10 s synthetic, 1280x720p60 H.264 + 3 Opus tracks, pink noise mix at -54.9 LUFS

youtube_4k60_fast.why: Same delivery shape on the RX 9070 XT's AMF encoder: minutes instead of an hour, for drafts you will actually upload unlisted to check. Fixed 80 Mbps so YouTube's re-encode has headroom.

measured.excerpt: 10 s synthetic, 1280x720p60 H.264 + 3 Opus tracks, pink noise mix at -54.9 LUFS

shorts_1080x1920.why: YouTube Shorts / TikTok / Reels. Center 9:16 crop of a 16:9 source by default (crop_x lets the studio follow the action); from a 4K source the 1215x2160 crop downsamples to 1080x1920 with no upscale.

measured.excerpt: 10 s synthetic, 1280x720p60 H.264 + 3 Opus tracks, pink noise mix at -54.9 LUFS

measured.note: the first AAC render read back at -1.4 dBTP (over -1.5); the re-render with the overshoot subtracted landed at -1.6

proxy_edit.why: Edit/scrub proxy for the web timeline (WebCodecs) and Kdenlive/Resolve: 1080p H.264 with a keyframe every 0.25 s so scrubbing never decodes 4 s of GOP. Never delivered.

measured.excerpt: 10 s synthetic, 1280x720p60 H.264 + 3 Opus tracks, pink noise mix at -54.9 LUFS

mezzanine_dnxhr.why: Intermediate for a hand-off to Resolve free or Blender when a long-GOP HEVC original is too heavy to scrub. DNxHR HQ 8-bit 4:2:2, PCM audio, all-intra. Large: plan on roughly 0.4-0.8 GB per minute at 4K60 (estimate, measure on first use).

measured.excerpt: 10 s synthetic, 1280x720p60 H.264 + 3 Opus tracks, pink noise mix at -54.9 LUFS

alpha_webm.why: Transparent overlay/sticker clip for the web and for compositing (VP9 with alpha). The answer to 'gifs transparent where we want': GIF has 1-bit alpha only.

measured.excerpt: 10 s synthetic, 640x360p30 ffv1 bgra, moving radial alpha

alpha_prores4444.why: Alpha overlay for Resolve/Blender/Kdenlive timelines (ProRes 4444 keeps an 8-16 bit alpha channel).

measured.excerpt: 10 s synthetic, 640x360p30 ffv1 bgra, moving radial alpha

alpha_webp_anim.why: Animated WebP with full 8-bit alpha: the 'transparent GIF' for chat, Discord and the web. Loops forever. Encoded with Pillow, not ffmpeg: ffmpeg's libwebp_anim piles up opacity on soft edges frame by frame (alpha error 39 by frame 1, 111 by frame 30, studio alpha smoke 2026-10-12); ffmpeg here cannot decode animated WebP either, so it is read back with Pillow too.

measured.excerpt: 10 s synthetic, 640x360p30 ffv1 bgra, moving radial alpha
